summary: Landable. No test or production code changed, so there is no mutation surface in the usual sense; the surface is the prose that governs my own output, and I mutated that instead. The load-bearing protection holds: both agent files re-state file:line, severity and the surviving mutation as non-overridable, and the skill's Never-cut list independently protects numbers, negations, code, file paths and caveats. The two detail classes named in the brief survive it -- 'under a frozen clock' is a caveat that changes what the reader would do, and '175/200 is a fixture artifact, not a production rate' is a number plus a negation, both explicitly protected. One clause I would want changed before it governs my output: the Never-cut list protects a number but not the PROVENANCE of a claim, and the Hedging clause on line 25 is the only pressure pointing the other way. Add 'the provenance of a claim -- measured, inferred, or not run' to Never-cut. Four minors, none blocking; per review.md minors-land they belong in the commit body, and fixing them is permitted and usually wrong. Separately, not a finding because I cannot observe the commit body: this adds a rung-6/7 prompt rule with no gate to layer 1, which AGENTS.md non-negotiable 9 says needs one sentence in the body saying why rungs 1-5 cannot carry it -- a style rule over model output is not a predicate over files in the tree, so the answer is probably 'it cannot', but it should be said.

findings.title: Never-cut protects numbers and caveats but not the provenance of a claim; the Hedging clause pushes the other way
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer writes 'I read the suite output rather than ran it, so this is inference' or 'check-mutants.sh does not exist, so that gate did not run'. Neither sentence contains a number, a negation from the line-40 list, code, a file path or an error string, and neither reads as a caveat that changes an action -- so none of the Never-cut categories on lines 37-44 names it. Line 25 does name it: it matches the shape of 'I'd probably recommend' and carries the instruction 'State the recommendation.' The qualifier is dropped, the finding is asserted flat, and non-negotiable 4 -- never claim a number was measured without measuring it -- has been degraded by the style rule rather than by a bad reviewer. Concrete surviving mutation of the staged prose: delete line 42 ('Caveats that change what the user would do') entirely and nothing in the tree notices -- no gate reads this file's body, check-portability reads frontmatter shape and check-links reads link targets, and both agent files re-enumerate only file:line, severity and the mutation, so the deletion changes no other file's meaning. The fix is one bullet: add provenance -- measured / inferred / not run -- to Never-cut.

findings.title: The skill's Out-of-scope list excludes 'reports'; its own description claims 'review report' as in-scope
findings.failure_scenario: Line 3 (frontmatter description, repeated verbatim in AGENTS.md:91 and .agents/skills/README.md:54) says 'Use when writing any reply, review report or finding.' Line 78-85 says these are out of scope and get 'normal, complete prose at natural length': 'Documentation, READMEs, reports, published artifacts', qualified by 'or persist beyond the conversation'. A review verdict is a report, is written for another agent, and persists in .harness/review/<sha>.<role>.json -- it satisfies the out-of-scope predicate on every clause while being named in-scope by the description. An agent invoking the skill directly via .claude/commands/brevity.md, which says 'write every reply that way for the rest of the session' and supplies no scoping, resolves the collision in whichever direction it read last, so the same skill produces two different output contracts. Surviving mutation: change line 85's 'reports' to 'review reports' and the description on line 3 is now word-for-word self-negating -- build-index.sh --check still passes (it compares index rows to frontmatter descriptions, not body text), check-portability still passes, check-links still passes. Nothing in the tree can tell the two versions apart. The reviewer agents are insulated because .claude/agents/*.md scope their use to 'output style: no preamble, no recap, no narration between tool calls', which is why this is minor and not major.

findings.title: Three tokenizer claims asserted in the present tense as measured fact, with no tokenizer named and no measurement anywhere in the tree
findings.failure_scenario: Lines 49-51 'The tokenizer splits them the same as the full word: zero tokens saved'; line 52 'An arrow is its own token; it saves nothing'; line 54 'sees and see are both one token'. All three are empirical, tokenizer-dependent, and stated flat. No tokenizer is named, no measurement is cited, and nothing in scripts/ or docs/ measures any of them. Surviving mutation: rewrite line 50 to 'saves roughly half the tokens', line 52 to 'an arrow is two tokens', line 54 to 'sees is two tokens and see is one' -- every gate still passes and no reader of this repository can falsify any version, because the evidence does not exist to check against. That is precisely the shape this project's own review.md refuses elsewhere: that file carries 'at least nine', 'at least 22 tasks', and a paragraph explaining why it quotes a floor rather than a denominator, because a number in a governing document is load-bearing. Minor rather than major because the three RULES the numbers support -- do not invent abbreviations, do not substitute arrows, do not mangle grammar -- are correct on readability grounds alone, so a reader who disbelieves the numbers still follows the rule. Fix is to state them as readability rules and drop the token arithmetic, or to measure and name the tokenizer.

findings.title: The new clause enumerates what 'stays, in full' and omits failure_scenario, the one field scripts/review.sh actually enforces
findings.failure_scenario: The staged line reads 'file:line, a severity, and the surviving mutation stay, in full.' scripts/review.sh record rejects any verdict whose finding lacks failure_scenario ('finding %d has no failure_scenario -- that makes it a style opinion'), and review.md rule failure-scenario makes it the thing that separates a finding from a style opinion. It is not in the protected list. A test-reviewer under brevity pressure keeps the mutation verbatim and compresses failure_scenario to a fragment; review.sh checks only non-emptiness, so it accepts it, the hash binds, and rule failure-scenario has degraded with every gate green. Surviving mutation, and I verified the code path rather than inferring it: set any finding's failure_scenario to a single word and review.sh record still writes the artifact and prints ok. The gap also exists in the pre-existing Output section at line 51-55, which likewise names only file:line, severity and the mutation -- so this line does not introduce the gap, but it is the line that newly asserts 'in full', which makes it the place the omission now reads as deliberate. Same wording applies to .claude/agents/reviewer.md:37, which does name 'the concrete failure scenario' and is therefore correct; the two clauses protect different sets and should protect the same one.
